newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dissident blasts army over security in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Dissident blasts army over security in Algeria.

text.p: Algeria's main secular opposition leader has accused the army, fighting a Moslem rebel insurgency, of devoting itself to shielding the country's rulers while paying only lip service to the security of ordinary Algerians.
Socialist Forces Front (FFS) chief Hocine Ait Ahmed, in a statement one day after about 20 suspected Moslem guerrillas slaughtered more than 30 civilians, including 11 women, said:
"I believe the security policy implemented by the army nowadays is not in the people's interest.
"It has been proved in more than one case that the army has not intervened to protect villages", said Ait Ahmed in an interview with the London-based Arab newspaper al Hayat, published on Thursday.
On Tuesday night, at least 31 people were slaughtered in the village of Sid el Kebir, near the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of the Algerian capital.

"So it appears from that, that the army security policy aims in the first place at protecting the people in power, their interests and economic facilities which are looked upon as a source for them to hold on in power, like gas and oil," said Ait Ahmed.
Tuesday night's killings, blamed by the authorities on Moslem fundamentalists, followed one over the weekend on another village where 11 women and three children had their throats cut.
More than 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
